back:
NPA proposes change → invites comments.
AMC/GM explain compliance and guidance.
EU regulation is then adopted.
tip: AMC = Acceptable Means of Compliance; GM = Guidance Material.

front: What is the overtaking rule?
back: The overtaking aircraft keeps clear and passes well clear.

front: Which aircraft categories have priority over powered aeroplanes in the lesson hierarchy?
back:
Airships, motor gliders, gliders and balloons.
Powered aircraft also give way to towing aircraft.
tip: Priority reflects relative manoeuvrability; apply specific rules.

front: What is the lesson’s order of priority among powered aircraft, airship, glider and balloon?
back: Balloon > glider/motor glider > airship > ordinary powered aircraft.
tip: Towing aircraft/object also receives protection from powered aircraft.

front: What should a powered aircraft do around aircraft towing another aircraft/object?
back: Give way.

front: What is the exact bank-keyed quirk in Q73?
back: Bank key: both engine-driven aircraft on crossing tracks divert right.
tip: This conflicts with the ordinary rule: aircraft with the other on its right gives way; flag and understand both.

front: What is the bank answer when a Boeing 737 and Cessna 152 cross in Class D?
back: Apply crossing priority: aircraft with the other on its right gives way.
tip: Do not assume the larger/commercial aircraft automatically has priority.

back: Height above the selected aerodrome datum.

back: 1013.25 hPa (standard pressure).

back: When climbing above the published transition altitude (TA).

front: When do you change from standard pressure to QNH on descent?
back: Below the published transition level (TL).
tip: Use published local TA/TL; never assume universal values.

front: What is the transition layer?
back: The layer between TA and TL.
tip: It separates altitude/QNH and flight-level/standard references.

back: Magnetic track/course, not heading.
tip: ATC instructions, route structure and published exceptions take precedence.

back: Add 500 ft to the corresponding thousand-foot level.

back: Horizontal footprint and vertical base/top.

front: What is a CTR?
back: Control Zone: surface-based controlled area around an aerodrome.

front: What is an AWY?
back: A published airway: three-dimensional corridor with defined vertical limits and class.
tip: Not merely a line on a map.

front: What is a FIR?
back: Flight Information Region; flight information and alerting services are provided.
tip: It is not itself an airspace class.

front: What should you read for a route’s temporary/restricted airspace?
back:
Check chart limits and AIP/NOTAM active times
and conditions; verify lateral and vertical profile.
tip: Also check weather and terrain.

front: What does Class A permit for VFR?
back: VFR is not permitted.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Airspace</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>VFR is not permitted.</text></svg>

front: What is the Class B VFR entry/separation headline in the sheet?
back: Clearance required; ATC separation from all aircraft.

front: What separation/traffic headline applies in Class C?
back: IFR separated from IFR and VFR; VFR separated from IFR; traffic information between VFR.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Airspace</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>IFR separated from IFR and VFR; VFR s</text></svg>

front: What is the Class D separation headline?
back: IFR separated from IFR; traffic information; VFR not separated from VFR.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Airspace</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>IFR separated from IFR; traffic infor</text></svg>

front: Does VFR in Class E receive separation from other traffic?
back: No separation for VFR; follow published procedures.
tip: Traffic information and separation are not the same.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Airspace</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>No separation for VFR; follow publish</text></svg>

front: What is the Class F/G headline for VFR?
back: Advisory/uncontrolled as designated; no ATC separation for VFR.
tip: Pilot maintains lookout and collision avoidance.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Airspace</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Advisory/uncontrolled as designated; </text></svg>

front: How do QNH, altitude and height relate to references?
back: QNH → altitude AMSL; QFE → height above local datum; 1013.25 → flight level.

front: Which units provide ATC and what do their abbreviations mean?
back: TWR: aerodrome; APP: approach; ACC: area control.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>ATS</text><rect x='45' y='62' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#2e8b57' opacity='0.18' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='81' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>TWR: aerodrome; APP: approach; ACC:</text></svg>

front: What does ATC do?
back: Controls traffic and provides separation/safe orderly conduct within its remit.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>ATS</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Controls traffic and provides separat</text></svg>

front: How does a pilot contact FIS, and what does it provide?
back:
By radio.
Flight information—not an ATC separation or clearance guarantee.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>ATS</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>By radio.</text><circle cx='51' cy='108' r='12' fill='#2e8b57'/><text x='51' y='112' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>2</text><text x='73' y='112' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Flight information—not an ATC separat</text></svg>

front: What service combination may a FIR provide in the bank?
back: FIS + alerting service (ALRS/ALR).

front: What does AIS publish?
back: Aeronautical information, including AIP and NOTAM products.
tip: AIS is not ATC.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>ATS</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Aeronautical information, including A</text></svg>

front: What is the difference between clearance and traffic information?
back: Clearance = permission; traffic information = advisory information, not separation.

front: What does RMZ require?
back: Continuously monitor the published frequency; if possible establish two-way communication.
tip: RMZ alone does not automatically require ATC clearance.

front: What must you do before entering a TMZ?
back: Select the required transponder, typically Mode A+C or Mode S as published.
tip: TMZ alone is not a clearance.

front: What is a TRA?
back: Temporary Reserved Airspace.
tip: Check published active times, vertical limits and conditions.

back: Assigned identity/code.
tip: Mode ≠ squawk code.

back: Pressure-altitude reporting.

front: What is Mode S?
back: Selective addressing; can transmit altitude and aircraft identity/data.

front: What is the common VFR conspicuity code listed?
back: 7000, where prescribed.
tip: Use the code required by current local procedures.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Transponder</text><path d='M75 132 A85 85 0 0 1 245 132' fill='none' stroke='#d7dee5' stroke-width='20'/><path d='M75 132 A85 85 0 0 1 160 55' fill='none' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='20'/><line x1='160' y1='132' x2='207' y2='80' stroke='#243447' stroke-width='4'/><circle cx='160' cy='132' r='7' fill='#243447'/><text x='160' y='177' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>7000, where prescribed.</text></svg>

front: What does squawk 7500 mean?
back: Unlawful interference.
tip: 75 = hijack/interference.

back: Radio communication failure.

back: Emergency.

back:
Prohibited: entry forbidden.
Restricted: entry only under conditions/permission.
Danger: activity may be hazardous.
tip: Restricted is the bank’s “cross with restrictions” answer.

back: Rectangular area on a land aerodrome prepared for aircraft landing and take-off.

front: What is aerodrome elevation?
back: Highest point of the landing area.

front: What is a taxi holding point?
back: Point where aircraft stop unless permission to proceed is given.
tip: A taxi clearance does not automatically cancel a runway holding instruction.

front: What is an aerodrome signal square for?
back: Ground area with symbols that visually inform overflying aircraft of aerodrome conditions.
tip: Not a place to taxi for clearances.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Aerodrome</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Ground area with symbols that visuall</text></svg>

front: What shape is a landing-direction indicator?
back: T-shaped.

front: From which direction does a windsock show the wind?
back: The direction from which the wind comes.
tip: A surrounding white circle can improve visibility.

front: What does an aerodrome beacon indicate?
back: Rotating beacon indicating the aerodrome’s location to pilots from the air.

front: How are runway numbers derived?
back: Magnetic runway direction rounded to nearest 10°; write as two digits.
tip: Example: 060° → runway 06.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway markings</text><circle cx='160' cy='106' r='57' fill='#eef5fa' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M160 45 L151 92 L160 85 L169 92 Z' fill='#2e8b57'/><path d='M160 167 L151 120 L160 127 L169 120 Z' fill='#c44536'/><text x='160' y='39' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' fill='#243447'>N</text><text x='160' y='187' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>RIGHT gives way when converging; head-on BOTH RIGHT</text></svg>

front: How are two parallel runways designated?
back: L and R: left and right (e.g. 06L / 06R).
tip: Three parallels may also use C for centre.

front: What colours are runway markings, edge lights and end lights?
back:
Markings: white.
Edge lights: white.
End lights: red.
tip: Taxiway signs/markings are generally yellow.

back: Glider flying in progress.

front: Yellow panel: left arrow + 2500 m. What does it mean?
back: 2,500 m runway is available from the intersection in the arrow’s direction.
tip: Not total runway length or distance to parking.

back: Visual aid to acquire and maintain the approach glidepath.

back:
4 red → well/too low.
3 red + 1 white → slightly low.
tip: More red = low.

front: PAPI: what do 1 red/3 white and 4 white mean?
back:
1 red + 3 white → slightly high.
4 white → well/too high.
tip: More white = high.

front: What is the upwind leg?
back: Climb after take-off, parallel and offset from the runway.

front: What is the crosswind leg?
back: Turn away from the runway track.
tip: It follows the upwind/departure portion.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Aerodrome circuit</text><path d='M65 70 H255 V125 H65 Z' fill='none' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M85 70 H235 M255 85 V112 M235 125 H85 M65 110 V85' fill='none' stroke='#d97706' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><text x='160' y='62' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#243447'>UPWIND</text><text x='265' y='101' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#243447'>CROSSWIND</text><text x='160' y='148' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#243447'>DOWNWIND</text><text x='55' y='101' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#243447'>BASE / FINAL</text><text x='160' y='182' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Trace local circuit arrows; direction varies</text></svg>

front: What is the downwind leg?
back: Parallel to the runway in the opposite direction.
tip: Circuit direction is local; check published procedure.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Aerodrome circuit</text><path d='M65 70 H255 V125 H65 Z' fill='none' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M85 70 H235 M255 85 V112 M235 125 H85 M65 110 V85' fill='none' stroke='#d97706' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><text x='160' y='62' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#243447'>UPWIND</text><text x='265' y='101' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#243447'>CROSSWIND</text><text x='160' y='148' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#243447'>DOWNWIND</text><text x='55' y='101' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#243447'>BASE / FINAL</text><text x='160' y='182' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Trace local circuit arrows; direction varies</text></svg>

front: What are base and final legs?
back:
Base turns toward final.
Final aligns with the runway for landing.

front: What is the departure leg and circuit decision point?
back:
Departure leg: continue after take-off before turning crosswind.
Decision point: choose continue downwind or turn base based on spacing/traffic/conditions.
tip: Trace arrows; circuit may be left- or right-hand.

front: Steady green light to aircraft in flight / on ground?
back:
Flight: cleared to land.
Ground: cleared for take-off.

back:

back:

back: Rock the wings.
tip: Use prescribed acknowledgement for the specified day/night context.

front: Alternating ailerons (normally left), then smooth turn left: meaning?
back: Follow me.
tip: Do not confuse with the “you may continue” manoeuvre.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Interception</text><circle cx='160' cy='106' r='57' fill='#eef5fa' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M160 45 L151 92 L160 85 L169 92 Z' fill='#2e8b57'/><path d='M160 167 L151 120 L160 127 L169 120 Z' fill='#c44536'/><text x='160' y='39' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' fill='#243447'>N</text><text x='160' y='187' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>RIGHT gives way when converging; head-on BOTH RIGHT</text></svg>

front: Abrupt 90°+ heading change and pull-up without crossing track: meaning?
back: You may continue your flight.
tip: Follow published procedures; contact the designated frequency/121.5 MHz as appropriate.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Interception</text><circle cx='160' cy='106' r='57' fill='#eef5fa' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M160 45 L151 92 L160 85 L169 92 Z' fill='#2e8b57'/><path d='M160 167 L151 120 L160 127 L169 120 Z' fill='#c44536'/><text x='160' y='39' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' fill='#243447'>N</text><text x='160' y='187' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>RIGHT gives way when converging; head-on BOTH RIGHT</text></svg>

front: What should you do when intercepted?
back:
Follow unmistakable instructions.
Attempt radio contact on the designated frequency,
including 121.5 MHz where appropriate.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Interception</text><rect x='12' y='77' width='86' height='55' rx='9' fill='#2f6f9f' opacity='0.2' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='2'/><text x='55' y='69' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#243447'>1</text><text x='55' y='100' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9' fill='#243447'>Follow unmistakabl</text><defs><marker id='a' markerWidth='6' markerHeight='6' refX='5' refY='3' orient='auto'><path d='M0 0 L6 3 L0 6 Z' fill='#52606d'/></marker></defs><text x='160' y='170' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#243447'>What should you do when intercepted?</text></svg>

front: What are the three alert phases?
back:
INCERFA = uncertainty.
ALERFA = alert.
DETRESFA = distress.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Emergency and SAR</text><rect x='45' y='62' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#2e8b57' opacity='0.18' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='81' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>INCERFA = uncertainty.</text><rect x='45' y='102' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#2f6f9f' opacity='0.18' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='121' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>ALERFA = alert.</text><rect x='45' y='142' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#d97706' opacity='0.18' stroke='#d97706' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='161' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>DETRESFA = distress.</text></svg>

front: How do you acknowledge a ground-to-air SAR signal in flight?
back: Rock the wings.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Emergency and SAR</text><circle cx='44' cy='95' r='13' fill='#2e8b57' stroke='#52606d' stroke-width='1'/><circle cx='95' cy='95' r='13' fill='#d97706' stroke='#52606d' stroke-width='1'/><circle cx='146' cy='95' r='13' fill='#c44536' stroke='#52606d' stroke-width='1'/><circle cx='197' cy='95' r='13' fill='#c44536' stroke='#52606d' stroke-width='1'/><circle cx='248' cy='95' r='13' fill='#eef5fa' stroke='#52606d' stroke-width='1'/><circle cx='299' cy='95' r='13' fill='#c44536' stroke='#52606d' stroke-width='1'/><text x='160' y='132' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>GREEN = permission / RED = stop or danger</text><text x='160' y='160' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>FLASH / STEADY changes meaning; know flight vs ground</text></svg>

front: Who can provide search-and-rescue service?
back: Civil and military organisations.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Emergency and SAR</text><rect x='25' y='58' width='128' height='93' rx='10' fill='#dbeafe' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='2'/><rect x='167' y='58' width='128' height='93' rx='10' fill='#dcfce7' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='89' y='80' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>DISTINGUISH</text><text x='231' y='80' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>APPLY</text><text x='89' y='112' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9' fill='#243447'>Civil and military organ</text></svg>

front: What are the three occurrence categories?
back: Incident → serious incident → accident.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Occurrence investigation</text><rect x='45' y='62' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#2e8b57' opacity='0.18' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='81' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Incident > serious incident > accid</text></svg>

front: What is the primary purpose of an aircraft accident investigation?
back:
Find causes, improve safety and make recommendations.
Not to assign guilt, civil liability or criminal blame.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Occurrence investigation</text><path d='M75 132 A85 85 0 0 1 245 132' fill='none' stroke='#d7dee5' stroke-width='20'/><path d='M75 132 A85 85 0 0 1 160 55' fill='none' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='20'/><line x1='160' y1='132' x2='207' y2='80' stroke='#243447' stroke-width='4'/><circle cx='160' cy='132' r='7' fill='#243447'/><text x='160' y='177' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Find causes, improve safety and make recom</text></svg>

front: What is DRY?
back: No visible moisture or contamination.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>No visible moisture or contamination.</text></svg>

front: What does DAMP mean?
back: Moisture changes the surface colour.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Moisture changes the surface colour.</text></svg>

front: What does WET mean?
back: Surface is soaked but has no significant standing-water patches.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Surface is soaked but has no signific</text></svg>

front: What are WATER PATCHES?
back: Visible patches of standing water.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Visible patches of standing water.</text></svg>

front: What threshold defines standing water in the sheet’s RCR matrix?
back: Depth over 3 mm.
tip: Use current RCR and aircraft performance data.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><path d='M75 132 A85 85 0 0 1 245 132' fill='none' stroke='#d7dee5' stroke-width='20'/><path d='M75 132 A85 85 0 0 1 160 55' fill='none' stroke='#c44536' stroke-width='20'/><line x1='160' y1='132' x2='207' y2='80' stroke='#243447' stroke-width='4'/><circle cx='160' cy='132' r='7' fill='#243447'/><text x='160' y='177' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Depth over 3 mm.</text></svg>

front: What does RCR report?
back: Runway condition for each third, in relevant ATS/AIS information.
tip: Reportable contaminants include water, snow, slush, ice, frost, chemicals and other contaminants/snowbanks.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><path d='M25 165 H295' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='4'/><rect x='48' y='102' width='78' height='63' fill='#dbeafe' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='2'/><rect x='142' y='70' width='76' height='95' fill='#ffedd5' stroke='#d97706' stroke-width='2'/><rect x='233' y='45' width='60' height='120' fill='#fee2e2' stroke='#c44536' stroke-width='2'/><text x='87' y='135' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>CTR</text><text x='180' y='112' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>TMA</text><text x='263' y='88' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>AWY</text><text x='160' y='188' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#243447'>Compare route footprint AND altitude / base / top</text></svg>

front: What is Rwy Condition Code 6?
back: Dry.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><rect x='45' y='62' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#2e8b57' opacity='0.18' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='81' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Dry.</text></svg>

front: What conditions give Code 5 in the lesson?
back:
Good: wet without significant standing water or frost.
Slush, dry snow or wet snow up to 3 mm.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><rect x='45' y='62' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#2e8b57' opacity='0.18' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='81' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Good: wet without significant stand</text></svg>

front: What does Code 4 indicate in the lesson?
back: Specially prepared winter runway / compacted snow below −15 °C; good to medium.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><rect x='45' y='62' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#2e8b57' opacity='0.18' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='81' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Specially prepared winter runway / </text></svg>

front: What does Code 3 indicate?
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><rect x='45' y='62' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#2e8b57' opacity='0.18' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='81' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Medium; braking/control noticeably </text></svg>

front: What does Code 2 indicate?
back: Medium to poor; e.g. standing water over 3 mm or slush over 3 mm.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><rect x='45' y='62' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#2e8b57' opacity='0.18' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='81' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Medium to poor; e.g. standing water</text></svg>

front: What does Code 1 indicate?
back: Poor: ice.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><rect x='45' y='62' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#2e8b57' opacity='0.18' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='81' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Poor: ice.</text></svg>

front: What does Code 0 indicate?
back: Less than poor: wet ice, water over compacted snow, or dry/wet snow over ice.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Runway condition</text><rect x='45' y='62' width='230' height='29' rx='7' fill='#2e8b57' opacity='0.18' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='160' y='81' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Less than poor: wet ice, water over</text></svg>

front: What are the three aircraft-light groups in the lesson?
back:
Anti-collision: rotating beacon/strobes.
Position: red/green/white.
Landing and taxi lights.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Lesson visual aids</text><circle cx='51' cy='70' r='12' fill='#2f6f9f'/><text x='51' y='74' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>1</text><text x='73' y='74' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Anti-collision: rotating beacon/strob</text><circle cx='51' cy='108' r='12' fill='#2e8b57'/><text x='51' y='112' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>2</text><text x='73' y='112' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Position: red/green/white.</text><circle cx='51' cy='146' r='12' fill='#d97706'/><text x='51' y='150' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#ffffff'>3</text><text x='73' y='150' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>Landing and taxi lights.</text></svg>

front: Where are aircraft position lights?
back: Red left wing; green right wing; white aft.
tip: They indicate orientation/conspicuity, not clearance.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Lesson visual aids</text><circle cx='160' cy='106' r='57' fill='#eef5fa' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M160 45 L151 92 L160 85 L169 92 Z' fill='#2e8b57'/><path d='M160 167 L151 120 L160 127 L169 120 Z' fill='#c44536'/><text x='160' y='39' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' fill='#243447'>N</text><text x='160' y='187' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>RIGHT gives way when converging; head-on BOTH RIGHT</text></svg>

front: What four reference distinctions prevent common Air Law mistakes?
back:
VFR vs VMC; AMSL vs AGL vs FL.
Flight vs ground visibility; clearance vs
information/separation.
tip: Read exact wording, including “NOT” and the altitude boundary.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect x='0' y='0' width='320' height='200' rx='14' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#243447'>Exam method</text><rect x='25' y='58' width='128' height='93' rx='10' fill='#dbeafe' stroke='#2f6f9f' stroke-width='2'/><rect x='167' y='58' width='128' height='93' rx='10' fill='#dcfce7' stroke='#2e8b57' stroke-width='2'/><text x='89' y='80' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>DISTINGUISH</text><text x='231' y='80' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#243447'>APPLY</text><text x='89' y='112' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9' fill='#243447'>VFR vs VMC; AMSL vs AGL </text></svg>

front: What does the bank’s Q5 stem caveat mean?
back:
Q5 is clipped after “appropriate papers for eve…”.
